_doc: CAL v1 floor points (lane S2). PLACED BY A CLAUDE AGENT FROM TRAIN KEYFRAMES (VISION), NOT BY A HUMAN (user decision U14 clause, Sun 18 Oct ~02:30: the user is asleep and delegated CAL to an agent). Each point was read by the agent on 2-3x zoomed crops, with a pixel grid, of the per-framing median background of A1+ TRAIN frames ($INTERCYCLE_DATA/cal/<framing>_bg.png, built by scripts/cal_v1.py gather; never committed) and checked against the people-masked click image out/cal_click/click_these/<framing>.jpg. uv = full-resolution pixel on the RAW (distorted) frame, at the centre line of the painted stripe; sigma_px = the agent's stated 1-sigma placement uncertainty (isotropic). No lengths are typed: none can be justified from the pictures. Floor relations (parallel / perp) refer to segments of two points, to traced lines of twin/cal/k1_hints_v1.json, or to the short stripe arms of 'line_hints' (hints placed by the agent, snapped to the sub-pixel stripe edge by intercycle.framing.trace_edge; a stripe arm's direction from its edge is far more precise than from two clicks). The zone frame: origin = 'origin' point, +z along 'axis' (in its pixel order), x = z turned 90 deg clockwise seen from above. c9_f0 and c9_f1 use the SAME physical origin (corner of the yellow L next to the green walkway) and the same axis (the walkway's left yellow line, top to bottom of the picture), so both framings map into one zone-9 frame; R2 (recess corner) is placed in both as a cross-check. NB: the click plan's c9_f1 points (cal_click_plan.json) were on a different physical L than its c9_f0 points (the recess beside the waste bins, ~400 px higher after the re-aim); this file fixes that. Rejected: vertical world edges (fence post, door frame, press columns) as roll constraints - their traces on the median background wandered (line RMS 3-5 px, one jumped edges), so they are not used.
